digest.component_or_area: LLM provider layer - Bedrock native integration
propositions: Rebar must provide a native Bedrock provider builder using pydantic-ai's BedrockConverseModel authenticated via AWS credential chain, avoiding an OpenAI-compatible gateway that loses prompt caching and native structured output

Prompt caching on Bedrock must be wired with exactly two keys (bedrock_cache_instructions, bedrock_cache_tool_definitions) for parity with the direct-Anthropic path, which sets only anthropic_cache_instructions and anthropic_cache_tool_definitions

Rebar must warn at INFO level when caching is requested but both cache_read_tokens and cache_write_tokens are zero with non-zero input_tokens, since cache failure is silent and bills full input on every call

The temperature parameter is fatal (400 ValidationException) on some Bedrock models (e.g. us.anthropic.claude-opus-4-7) but not others (e.g. us.anthropic.claude-sonnet-4-6), requiring per-model capability overrides keyed on exact model id rather than provider name

Model-id-specific 400 errors mentioning sampling parameters (temperature, top_p, top_k) and rejection words (deprecated, unsupported) must be caught and translated to LLMConfigError naming the model id, offending parameter, and both remedies, never swallowing unrelated 400s

The Bedrock builder and all boto3-dependent code must be gated behind an optional [bedrock] extra so pip install nava-rebar[agents] has no AWS dependency, while [bedrock] is added to the dev extra so unit tests run in CI with boto3 mocked
